rationale.conceptual: The paper applies standard DFT (GGA-PBE) and quasiharmonic approximation, which are well-established but require non-trivial understanding of phonon calculations, free-energy fitting, and mode Grüneisen parameter extraction. It is an established, multi-part method, not a simple textbook operation.
rationale.execution: The agent must run a pipeline of several dependent stages: unit-cell geometry optimization, 15-volume static energy scan, supercell phonon force calculations (108 atoms) at each volume, post-processing with PHONOPY, and QHA fitting. Orchestrating Quantum ESPRESSO, managing many files, and handling a long compute run make it a fragile, multi-tool orchestration.

difficulty.reasoning: The task reproduces anisotropic negative thermal expansion and Grüneisen parameters of LaC2 via DFT+quasiharmonic approximation. The method is an established multi-component workflow (geometry optimization, volume scan, supercell phonon calculations, free-energy minimization, EOS fitting) that requires careful implementation but is not novel. The execution involves orchestrating Quantum ESPRESSO and PHONOPY across many volumes and supercell force evaluations, making it a long multi-stage pipeline.

compute_estimate.reasoning: DFT plane-wave calculations on a 108-atom supercell over 15 volumes require extensive CPU time (estimated 24-48 hours) and moderate RAM (a few GB per core); no GPU needed. Input data is negligible (crystal structure and pseudopotentials).
